catalog.summary: Site sections that open panels of links.

patternStatus: Read on 2026-10-01 from the rendered example page. The example's own note says it uses the word menu in the colloquial sense and does not use the menu role, because a site's navigation does not need the keyboard the menu and menubar pattern specify; no menu, menubar or menuitem role is written here. The keyboard table transcribes the example's Keyboard Support section, its optional arrow keys, Home and End included, without a roving tabindex: every top-level control stays a tab stop.

roles.reason: Every role but group is the element's own: nav > ul > li > (button + div) and (a), the disclosure example's structure. A nested root is a div with no landmark, because a navigation landmark inside a navigation landmark is announced twice. group carries role=group and aria-labelledby to its group-label, so a column's title names the links under it

element.label: span
element.reason: The root is a nav where the family stands alone and a div where it is nested in another navigation-menu's content. The trigger is always a native button: it owns aria-expanded and aria-controls, and the family wires it

anatomy.root: the nav landmark, aria-label from messages.navigation unless the consumer wrote one. position: relative: the viewport and every content are placed against it. data-orientation, data-size, and data-nested when inside another root
anatomy.list: the sections and the top-level links, in a row or in a column
anatomy.item: one section — a trigger followed by its content — or one top-level link. data-value names it; data-open while its content is shown
anatomy.trigger: a native button: aria-expanded, aria-controls pointing at content, data-open while open, data-current while its content holds the current link. The control scale's height, inset and type
anatomy.indicator: the chevron-down Glyph element at the trigger's end, a half turn while open; chevron-right with a directional box in a vertical root
anatomy.link: a destination, at the top level beside the triggers or inside a content. aria-current=page and data-current when current; aria-disabled with the activation refused when disabled
anatomy.content: one section's panel, after its trigger in the same li. hidden while closed; data-open, data-motion while it crosses another. A query container whose inline size is stated, columns times the column size, capped by the space available
anatomy.links: the grid of links inside a content or a group; its columns come from the content's data-columns and fall to one below 480 pixels of content
anatomy.group: a column of the panel with a title: role=group and aria-labelledby to group-label
anatomy.group-label: a group's title in the small type and the muted ink
anatomy.icon: a rich link's mark, aligned to the text of its label
anatomy.label: a rich link's title
anatomy.description: a rich link's description: two lines to the eye, whole in the DOM
anatomy.footer: the panel's last row, under a rule: the consumer's call to action
anatomy.viewport: the shared surface: ground, edge, shadow and radius, sized and placed from the measured content. data-open, and data-positioned once the script has placed it. Without script it is not drawn and the open content paints its own surface
anatomy.arrow: a mark on the viewport's edge pointing at the open trigger, sliding from trigger to trigger. Rendered only when arrow is true

content.inItemReason: The content stays after its trigger in the DOM, as the disclosure example places it, and is laid over the viewport's box with no ground of its own. Tab reaches it without the sentinels Radix and Base UI add after porting the content into the viewport, and React ports nothing. Cost: a consumer who clips the root with overflow: hidden clips the panel
content.mounted: always: a closed content is hidden, not removed. The tab sequence, a static render and a search engine read the destinations. A consumer who wants a heavy panel lazy renders its children only while value names it

runtimeProperties.--slotted-navigation-menu-viewport-inlin: from the root's inline start to the viewport's: under a trigger, the trigger's inline start moved toward the start until the viewport fits; beside a column, the column's width
runtimeProperties.--slotted-navigation-menu-viewport-block: vertical only: from the root's top to the open trigger's top beside it, or to its bottom under it
runtimeProperties.--slotted-navigation-menu-arrow-offset: the open trigger's centre, measured from the viewport's inline start
runtimeProperties.--slotted-navigation-menu-available-inli: the widest a panel may be: the window's inline size less a gutter at each side under a trigger, or the room at the column's end beside it

runtimePropertiesReason: Values a stylesheet needs and only script can measure are custom properties under the name that says so (docs/build-briefing.md). They are runtime values, not design tokens, and are written on the root

hover.open: a pointer resting on a trigger for openDelay opens its section with the reason pointer
hover.switch: with a section open, a pointer entering another trigger switches without the delay
hover.close: a pointer leaving the root closes after closeDelay, cancelled when it returns
hover.touch: a pointer whose pointerType is touch never opens by hover: a touch is a click
hover.reason: Radix and Ark wait 200 milliseconds to open and Ark 300 to close; Base UI waits 50 for both, which opened a panel under a pointer crossing the bar on its way elsewhere. The delays are behaviour, not motion, and do not come from the duration scale

keyboard.effect: moves to the next control: each trigger and top-level link, and the links of an open content after its trigger
moves to the previous control under the same rule
toggles a trigger's section and asks value to move with the reason keyboard; follows a link, and with closeOnSelect asks value to move to null with the reason select
toggles a trigger's section like Enter; on a link the platform scrolls the page, and the family writes nothing over it
closes the open section through dismissable-layer with the reason escape
keyboard.focus: the trigger of the section that closed

keyboard.effect: horizontal, on an open trigger: enters the content; on a closed trigger or a top-level link in a vertical root: the next top-level control; inside a content: the next focusable of the content
keyboard.focus: the content's first focusable, the next top-level control, or the next focusable of the content

keyboard.effect: inside a content: the previous focusable, and from the first the trigger; on a top-level control of a vertical root: the previous one
keyboard.focus: the previous focusable, or the trigger

keyboard.effect: horizontal, on a top-level control: the next one, and the first from the last; vertical, on an open trigger: enters the content
keyboard.focus: the next top-level control, or the content's first focusable

keyboard.effect: horizontal, on a top-level control: the previous one, and the last from the first. Mirrored in rtl
on a top-level control: the first one; inside a content: its first focusable
keyboard.focus: the first top-level control, or the content's first focusable

keyboard.effect: on a top-level control: the last one; inside a content: its last focusable
keyboard.focus: the last top-level control, or the content's last focusable

keyboardReason: The disclosure example lists the arrows, Home and End as optional, for keyboard users without a screen reader. They are adopted as a shortcut over the tab sequence, not as a replacement: no roving tabindex, every top-level control stays a tab stop, and movement by arrow keys does not animate
focusLeaves: focus leaving the root closes the open section with the reason blur; focus moving between top-level controls leaves it open, as in the disclosure example

current.trigger: a trigger whose content holds the current link carries data-current, so the reader sees which section they are in with every section closed
current.painted: the link's ground in --slotted-tone-accent-surface under --slotted-tone-accent-text, with --slotted-current-edge: the pair top-navigation and side-navigation draw. A current trigger takes the accent ink and keeps its resting ground

disabled.trigger: the native disabled attribute; the section never opens
disabled.link: aria-disabled=true, the click refused, the href kept — list-item's rule
disabled.item: data-disabled, never aria-disabled, which ARIA 1.2 deprecates on listitem

nested.rule: a root inside another root's content renders a div, writes no landmark, is vertical, and draws no viewport: its list is a column at the panel's start and its open section stands beside it on the outer panel's surface, so a second level switches inside the same panel

dataAttributes.data-positioned: on the viewport once the script has measured and placed it
dataAttributes.data-columns: on content: 1, 2 or 3 columns of links
dataAttributes.data-nested: on a root inside another root's content
dataAttributes.data-placement: on a vertical root: beside while the column has room at its end for the open panel, below when it has none and the panel drops under the trigger

open.reason: Which section is open: the data-value of its item, or null. pointer is a click or a hover with a mouse or a pen; keyboard is Enter or Space on a trigger; escape and outsidePress come from dismissable-layer; blur is focus leaving the root; select is a content link activated while closeOnSelect holds

menuRole.reason: Radix, Base UI and Ark render no menu role either; the APG example's own note refuses it for site navigation. A list of commands is the menu family

backdrop.reason: Base UI ships one. A navigation panel is not modal and does not dim the page; a consumer who wants it writes [data-ui='navigation-menu']:has([data-part='viewport'][data-open])::after in two declarations

feature.reason: Radix's demonstration opens with a large card. It is the card family inside a content: a Card rendered as an a in a links cell with grid-row: span 3

portal.reason: Radix and Base UI port the content into the viewport and rebuild the tab order with sentinels. The content stays in its li here, which is the disclosure example's own structure (content.inItemReason)

navigationMenu.defaultsReason: Axis defaults and the hover delays. The uncontrolled start is defaultValue, in React alone: Angular ships one model() for value

indicator.closed: chevron-down in a horizontal root, chevron-right in a vertical one
indicator.open: chevron-down turned half a turn; in a vertical root chevron-right does not turn, because the section opens beside the trigger, where it already points
indicator.rtl: chevron-down is not mirrored; chevron-right is, through directional on its icon box

placement.rule: a vertical root's panel opens beside the column while the column has room at its end, and drops under the open trigger when it has none, rather than clipping at the window's edge; the chevron turns a quarter to point at it
placement.reason: Measured at 240 pixels: a 13rem column left no room at its end, and the panel beside it was clipped to 50 pixels

composedBy.top-navigation: the bar's nav part carries the root and its items are sections; a section folded into the bar's overflow panel opens its content in line there, the surface stays away, hover does not open it, and focus or a press inside that content is not outside the menu
